newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures ends up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures ends up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up across the board on Tuesday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at an intra-day low of 23,780 yuan ($2,867) per tonne, rising 90 yuan. It opened at 23,880 and hit a high of 23,920.
May rose 30 to 23,280, June 80 to 23,580, July 80 to 23,680, September 100 to 23,790 and October 170 to 23,750.
Combined volume rose to 41,480 tonnes from 20,900.
Copper opened up but profit-taking pushed the contracts down for most of the session with most of them ending at or near their intra-day lows, traders said.
Traders said LME gains helped boost confidence of long position holders but many investors were reluctant to follow.

"Many investors did not believe copper would rise or fall sharply in the short term, leading to a lack of follow-up buying," one trader said. "They took advantage of LME gains to liquidate long positions at high levels."
Traders said a lack of funds was also an important factor.
"Some investors were eager to offset their long positions to move money to the booming stock markets," a second trader said.
Physical prices are now moving between 23,300 yuan and 23,400 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area.
Traders said they expected copper to move in a range between 23,500 and 24,000 in the next few days.
Aluminium ended mostly up. May rose 30 to 15,310, June 50 to 15,600, July 30 to 15,880 and August fell 30 to 16,020. Combined volume rose to 2,560 tonnes from 980. ($1 =8.2932 yuan)
